relations.subject: Gunapala Piyasena Malalasekera
relations.evidence: By following a correspondence course from England, he gained a BA from the University of London External System in 1919 with a first division.

relations.subject: Gunapala Piyasena Malalasekera
relations.evidence: In 1923, he proceeded to join the University of London and obtained the two postgraduate degrees of a MA and a PhD concurrently in 1925, in oriental languages majoring in Pali from the London School of Oriental Studies.

relations.subject: Gunapala Piyasena Malalasekera
relations.evidence: Malalasekera would later gain a DLitt in 1938, his thesis was 'Pali Literature in Sri Lanka' from the University of London.

relations.subject: Gunapala Piyasena Malalasekera
relations.evidence: In 1927, he succeeded Ven. Suriyagoda as lecturer in the then University College, Colombo to lecture in English on Sinhala, Pali and Sanskrit for the University of London degree examinations.

relations.subject: Gunapala Piyasena Malalasekera
relations.evidence: In 1927, he succeeded Ven. Suriyagoda as lecturer in the then University College, Colombo to lecture in English on Sinhala, Pali and Sanskrit for the University of London degree examinations.

relations.subject: Gunapala Piyasena Malalasekera
relations.role: Professor of Pali and Buddhist Studies
relations.evidence: When the University of Ceylon was founded in 1942, he became the Professor of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

relations.subject: Gunapala Piyasena Malalasekera
relations.role: Dean of the Faculty of Oriental Studies
relations.evidence: Serving as the Head of the Department of Pali, he went on to serve as the Dean of the Faculty of Oriental Studies, University of Ceylon.

relations.subject: Gunapala Piyasena Malalasekera
relations.evidence: On his departure from the University of Ceylon, he was appointed Professor Emeritus.
